subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Before the Big Bang
description: A quick win: understand Before the Big Bang.

hook.text: What existed before the Big Bang? Time itself may have begun at that moment, making 'before' meaningless.

buildup.text: Stephen Hawking compared it to asking what's south of the South Pole. There is no 'south' beyond that point.

discovery.text: Some models propose a bouncing universe—an earlier universe collapsed and rebounded as our Big Bang.

twist.text: Roger Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology suggests Big Bangs repeat endlessly in an infinite chain of universes.

climax.text: These ideas are speculative and currently untestable. What came before may remain forever beyond our reach.

punchline.text: Before the beginning. The ultimate question without an answer—yet.

quiz.question: Why is the question 'what came before the Big Bang' problematic?
options: Time itself may have begun at the Big Bang, making 'before' meaningless
We know exactly what came before but the answer is classified
The Big Bang was actually a slow process, not a single event

details.summary: What happened before the Big Bang is physics' deepest question. Standard cosmology says time itself began with the Big Bang, making 'before' meaningless.
details.whyItMatters: This question probes the ultimate limits of scientific knowledge. Whether time has a beginning, whether our universe arose from something else, and whether we can ever know — these questions define the frontier of cosmology and physics.
takeaways: Standard cosmology says time began with the Big Bang
Alternative models propose prior universes or quantum origins
This remains physics' deepest unanswered question

faq.question: Could the universe have come from nothing?
faq.answer: Some physicists argue yes — in quantum mechanics, 'nothing' is unstable. Quantum fluctuations in a vacuum can spontaneously produce particle-antiparticle pairs.

faq.question: What is the Big Bounce theory?
faq.answer: Loop quantum gravity suggests the Big Bang was actually a Big Bounce — a previous universe contracted to extreme density, then quantum gravity effects prevented a singularity and caused a rebound. This avoids the singularity problem and potentially allows an infinite sequence of bouncing universes.
